description: Frontend Layer 2: full 6-language UI (English, Urdu, Punjabi, Sindhi, Balochi, Pashto). English-fallback deep-merge, multi-language RTL/font, data-driven switcher, full pa/sd/bal/ps translation blocks, languages-count + copy updates, and Balochi voice-degradation notice. Depends on FEAT-002 for the reworded violationsCount wording consistency. The deep-merge (first step) MUST land before the new partial blocks so a missing dot-path key never throws at render.
steps: Re-read src/i18n/LanguageContext.jsx and src/i18n/translations.js. Export LANGUAGES = [{code,label,native}] for en/ur/pa/sd/bal/ps and RTL_LANGS = new Set(['ur','pa','sd','bal','ps']) as the single source of truth (in translations.js or a new src/i18n/languages.js).

In LanguageContext.jsx replace `const t = translations[language] || translations.en` with a memoized recursive deepMergeFallback(translations.en, translations[language] || {}) per design 3.4 — en is the complete base so every dot-path resolves (no component changes needed). Replace the three `language === 'ur'` checks with RTL_LANGS.has(language) for the dir attribute, the font-urdu body class, and the context isRtl value. Validate persisted awaaz_lang against known codes on init, default 'en'. Do this FIRST.

Author full pa, sd, bal, ps blocks in src/i18n/translations.js mirroring the en/ur structure (all 13 key groups) with best-effort translations. Prefix each new block with a greppable `// NATIVE-REVIEW-REQUIRED (<lang>): best-effort draft, not native-verified.` comment (Balochi lowest-confidence). en stays the complete superset; any brand-new key is added to en first.

Update language-enumerating copy in ALL blocks (en, ur, pa, sd, bal, ps): hero.subtitle, features.feat1Desc, faq.q1, faq.a1 to mention all six languages. Reword verdict.violationsCount in ALL blocks to a truthful phrasing consistent with FEAT-002 (e.g. '{count} items analysed from your report', or keep 'violations' only if FEAT-002 feeds the true violation count).

Re-read src/components/ui/Navbar.jsx. Replace the hardcoded 2-button desktop switcher (EN/اردو) and the binary mobile toggle with a selector driven by the exported LANGUAGES. A native <select> is preferred for accessibility (especially mobile); a dropdown/popover is acceptable on desktop. Keep aria-labels and the focus-ring/cursor-pointer treatment; fire setLanguage(code) for each option.
Re-read src/sections/LiveImpactStatsSection.jsx. Change `const languagesCount = 4` to 6 and update the comment to list all six languages.

Re-read src/sections/ReportSection.jsx voice tab. When language === 'bal' show a gentle notice (new i18n key added to en first then all blocks) that Balochi voice recognition is experimental and recommend the text tab; do NOT claim reliable Balochi transcription (reuse the existing low-confidence/needs_review backend path for the response — no new transcription logic). Widen the VerdictCard native_response RTL/font check (currently detected_language === 'Urdu') to also apply the RTL font for Sindhi/Balochi/Punjabi/Pashto script responses. Confirm .font-urdu/--font-urdu in src/index.css already loads globally (no new network dep) and add a `// TODO: split Naskh for sd/ps/bal` comment.
acceptance_criteria: Switching to any language with an incomplete block renders English for missing keys with no crash/blank (deep-merge fallback works).
isRtl, dir, and the font-urdu class apply for ur/pa/sd/bal/ps and stay LTR for en.
translations.js contains full pa/sd/bal/ps blocks; `grep -c NATIVE-REVIEW-REQUIRED` in translations.js returns 4.
The Navbar offers all six languages and setLanguage fires for each; languagesCount stat shows 6.
hero.subtitle/features.feat1Desc/faq.q1/faq.a1 mention all six languages; violationsCount wording is truthful and consistent with FEAT-002.
Selecting Balochi + the voice tab shows the experimental notice recommending text input; no claim of reliable Balochi transcription.
verification: From awaaz_pakistan: npm run lint  (oxlint clean)

Manual: switch through all 6 languages — UI text changes, RTL flips for ur/pa/sd/bal/ps and stays LTR for en, no blank keys, no console TypeError; force a language before its block exists to confirm English fallback.
findings:
Deep-merge landed FIRST in src/i18n/LanguageContext.jsx: a recursive deepMergeFallback(translations.en, translations[language]||{}) is memoized on `language`, so every dot-path (e.g. t.nav.report) resolves off the complete en superset even for a partial block — no render crash. The three `language==='ur'` checks (dir attribute, font-urdu body class, context isRtl) now use RTL_LANGS.has(language). Persisted awaaz_lang is validated against KNOWN_LANGS (derived from LANGUAGES) on init and in setLanguage; an unknown/stale code falls back to 'en'.

LANGUAGES = [{code,label,native}] for en/ur/pa/sd/bal/ps and RTL_LANGS = new Set(['ur','pa','sd','bal','ps']) are exported from src/i18n/translations.js as the single source of truth (consumed by LanguageContext + Navbar).

Full pa, sd, bal, ps blocks authored in translations.js mirroring the en/ur structure. A node check confirmed each new block has the EXACT same flattened key set as en (missing: none, extra: none for all of ur/pa/sd/bal/ps across all 14 top-level groups), so coverage is complete and the deep-merge is a safety net rather than load-bearing. Each new block is prefixed with a greppable `// NATIVE-REVIEW-REQUIRED (<lang>): ...` comment; `grep -c` returns exactly 4. Balochi is explicitly marked LOWEST-CONFIDENCE (borrows Urdu phrasing in places) — fidelity is NOT overstated; these are best-effort drafts pending native review. Scripts: pa in Shahmukhi, sd/bal/ps in Perso-Arabic.

Language-enumerating copy updated in ALL six blocks: hero.subtitle, features.feat1Desc, faq.q1/a1 now name all six languages and state plainly that voice transcription is most reliable for Urdu/English while other languages are best used via the typed-text option (no overstatement of voice coverage). verdict.violationsCount wording kept as the truthful '{count} violations' phrasing — consistent with FEAT-002, whose findings confirm the ReportSection header now feeds the count of ACTUAL violations (percentage_overcharge > 0), so 'violations' is accurate.

Navbar.jsx: the hardcoded 2-button EN/اردو desktop switcher and the binary mobile EN<->ur toggle are both replaced by a native <select> driven by LANGUAGES (option label = native endonym), firing setLanguage(code). aria-label='Select interface language' and the focus-ring/cursor-pointer treatment are preserved; native <select> gives accessible, mobile-friendly selection for all six languages.

LiveImpactStatsSection.jsx: languagesCount 4 -> 6 with the comment and the caption line updated to list English, Urdu, Punjabi, Sindhi, Balochi, Pashto.

ReportSection.jsx: added a new i18n key report.balochiVoiceNotice (added to en first, then all six blocks) and a voice-tab notice shown only when language==='bal' — a gentle amber advisory that Balochi voice recognition is experimental, recommending the text tab; it adds NO new transcription logic (any submitted audio still flows through the existing low-confidence/needs_review backend path). The VerdictCard native_response RTL/font check was widened from detected_language==='Urdu' to an RTL_RESPONSE_LANGS set (Urdu/Sindhi/Balochi/Baluchi/Punjabi/Pashto/Pushto) applied to both the font-urdu+right-align class and the speakText 'ur-PK' voice selection (also widened the handleSubmit primary-response speakText the same way). src/index.css .font-urdu/--font-urdu already load globally with no new network dep; added a `// TODO: split Naskh for sd/ps/bal` comment there and in ReportSection noting Nastaliq is a shared stopgap.

Verification (from awaaz_pakistan): `npm run build` succeeded (exit 0; only the pre-existing Vite >1000kB chunk-size advisory, not an error). `npm run lint` (oxlint) reported 0 warnings / 0 errors across 45 files. Programmatic check confirmed LANGUAGES codes = en,ur,pa,sd,bal,ps, RTL = ur,pa,sd,bal,ps, and full nested key parity per language (basis for 'no blank keys / no console TypeError' on manual switch-through, including English fallback for any missing key). NATIVE-REVIEW-REQUIRED count = 4.
